bug_semantics: FluentCMS File Management stores uploaded SVG bytes unsanitized and later serves them with the client-supplied MIME type image/svg+xml. FileController.Upload copies formFile.ContentType and the raw stream into FileService.Create, which persists via fileStorageProvider.Upload with no SVG sanitization. FileController.Download then returns Results.File(..., contentType: file.ContentType). The frontend maps unauthenticated GET /files/* through RemoteFileProviderMiddleware, which fetches that download using the app API token and copies Content-Type onto the response without Content-Disposition: attachment or CSP, so a browser navigating to the public file URL executes embedded <script>, on* handlers, or javascript: URIs. Authenticated admin upload plus visitor (including guest) fetch is the stored XSS path in issue #2404.

potential_fix.approach: In FileService.Create, detect SVG by extension/content-type and sanitize the stream before fileRepository.Create/fileStorageProvider.Upload: parse as XML with DTD prohibited, strip script and foreignObject elements, strip on* event-handler attributes, and strip href/xlink:href/src/action values using javascript:, vbscript:, or data: schemes; replace unparseable SVG with an empty <svg>. Optionally also serve image/svg+xml with CSP sandbox or Content-Disposition: attachment.
potential_fix.rationale: The sink is stored executable SVG served as image/svg+xml. Removing script/event/javascript: payloads before persistence closes the stored XSS even when /files middleware copies the original Content-Type to unauthenticated visitors.
